parsed.title: Discussion on tax filing, domain purchase, and app viability

claims.text: Paying 500 UAH to a contact (Sveta) helped avoid larger penalties from incorrectly marked columns in declarations
The inspector had not reviewed declarations for 1.5 years and was later disciplined, leading to a thorough re‑check of all years' declarations
Correct re‑filing cost about 1 000 UAH, which was cheaper than paying all fines
The main difficulty is not calculating taxes themselves but ensuring each column is correctly matched and subtracted
The whole procedure typically takes about an hour with Excel, possibly one day maximum
Quarterly reports must be submitted and taxes paid correctly
User P2 has not bought a domain yet
P1 sarcastically suggests someone buying a calculator will have money for a domain
P4 doubts anyone will buy the domain, calling it a useless item
P4 later describes the domain as a “silly thing” that won’t evaporate even in heat
Web platforms are the easiest to build but less profitable than Android/iOS apps
SEO performance is poor; the site does not appear even on the 10th Google page
No external traffic from social platforms or contextual ads; app stores promote new apps more effectively
No passive ad revenue from the website and user retention is nearly zero due to early paywalls
Conversion is presumed near zero because the product does not simplify enough or integrate with banks or tax cabinets
Successful similar projects use fast delivery (< 1 week) and cross‑platform stacks like Flutter, copying popular ideas with minor tweaks
P1 doubts the market will buy such a product, betting it won’t sell in months
